newsitem.title: USA: UPS says set for "businesslike" talks with union.
newsitem.headline: UPS says set for "businesslike" talks with union.

text.p: United Parcel Service negotiators were set to reconvene contract talks with the Teamsters union in a "businesslike" mood, a UPS spokeswoman said Friday.
"At this point we are diligently working," UPS spokeswoman Gina Ellrich told reporters. "The mood is absolutely serious -- it's very businesslike."
Ellrich said there had been no further developments in the talks and reiterated that UPS had made its "last, best and final" offer.
She added that hundreds of thousands of packages had been diverted to other carriers since the union contract expired Thursday.
"We have seen between yesterday and today hundreds of thousands of packages diverted," she said.
The company notified customers on Tuesday that it could not guarantee delivery once the contract expired. UPS carries about 12 million packages a day, Ellrich said.

Union representatives had threatened to call a strike when the contract ran out at midnight (0400 GMT) on Thursday, but postponed any action to allow for further talks. The talks were set to start at 1 p.m. EDT on Friday.
